summary: Helmond is moving parking out of the streets of its centre and into garages at the edge of the core shopping area under its Centrum 2030 programme, the Mobiliteitsvisie Helmond 2040 and the Strategie Parkeren (colophon June 2025). On-street parking costs 2.65 euros per hour in all five tariff classes since 1 January 2026, with a 4.00 euro daily maximum in class 5, resident permits cost 15.80 euros per month in the Centrum and Schil zones, and the pedestrian zone has been camera-enforced since 1 November 2023. The municipal garages Doorneind and Boscotondo sell residents', business and 24/7 subscriptions for 47.50 to 125.90 euros per month in 2026, and the council approved 21.2 million euros in April 2025 to buy and extend the Elzas garage, with about 250 extra spaces under Piet Blomplein planned to start building in 2028. The municipality intends to introduce paid parking in De Waart, Kasteel Noord, Suytkade and Annabuurt in 2027; its own strategy says garages are busiest on Saturday and Sunday afternoons with ample spare capacity at other times, and plans a discounted station park-and-ride tariff. A parking guidance system initially covers only Boscotondo and Doorneind, about 250 extra public charge points are planned by 2028, Gepast Parkeren card readers on the street stopped working from 1 October 2026, and Q-Park runs the 170-space P+R Smalstraat at the station (NS lists 0.99 euros per hour, 6.00 per day and 4.00 for rail travellers from 1 May 2026).

items.text: The council adopted the Verordening parkeerbelastingen Helmond 2026 on 4 November 2025; it applies from 1 January 2026 and sets 2.65 euros per hour in all five on-street tariff classes, with a 4.00 euro daily maximum in class 5. The additional assessment for unpaid parking is 73.55 euros plus one hour of the local tariff and the wheel-clamp fee is 59.70 euros.

Under the 2026 ordinance, residents' permits cost 15.80 euros per month in the Centrum and Schil zones and 5.25 euros in Overig; business permits cost 94.60 euros in Centrum and Schil and 15.80 euros in Overig. A street-parking permit in tariff classes 4 and 5 is 94.60 euros per month, and holders of a disabled parking card may park twice as long for the hourly fee.

The Beleidsregel Parkeernormen Helmond 2024 for the Centrum, Stationskwartier and Kernwinkelgebied (published 11 September 2024) lets the council exempt conversions to housing in the core shopping area (up to 6 units per address) from providing car spaces on site, but those residents then have no right to a municipal permit or garage subscription.
items.source_title: Beleidsregel Parkeernormen Helmond 2024 - Centrum, stationskwartier en kernwinkelgebied (Gemeenteblad 2024, 388156)

items.text: The Strategie Parkeren (colophon June 2025; PDF file created 9 February 2026) sets out locate, norm and tariff principles: phase out street spaces in the core and move visitors and residents to garages at the edge of the centre, start from 15,000 homes and jobs by 2040, and stop new residents of the centre from getting street permits. It is a strategy to be turned into an Agenda Parkeren, not a final rule set.

For the station area the Strategie Parkeren states that paid parking should apply everywhere with an hourly rate not below garage rates, and that more parking capacity next to the station is intended in time. It also proposes studying a P+R tariff structure with a discount for rail travellers, possibly with NS.

For the ring around the centre the Strategie Parkeren proposes paid parking instead of blue zones, for example with the first two hours free but registration required, so that scan-car enforcement can be used. Paid spaces are enforced by scan car (fines go to the municipality), while permit and wrong-parking checks by officers are costly.

The Strategie Parkeren says visitor demand in the existing centre garages peaks on Saturday and Sunday afternoons and that outside those peaks there is ample spare capacity, which residents and workers could use. It expects weekend spare capacity to become very limited within a few years, and notes that garage capacity is not yet enough to move all residents off the street.

The Centrum 2030 page (read on 21 October 2026, undated) says parking is being moved from streets to garages such as Elzas, Boscotondo, Doorneind and Ameidewal, with about 10,000 homes planned in and around the centre. It reports that much of the centre already has a waiting list for a street-parking permit and that permits will get harder to obtain.
items.source_title: Veranderingen in parkeren centrum Helmond (Gemeente Helmond)

items.text: The Centrum 2030 page 'Verplaatsen' (read on 21 October 2026, undated) states the intention to introduce paid parking in De Waart, Kasteel Noord, Suytkade and Annabuurt in 2027, and at Ons Oostende/Ons Willem in 2029 when that project is finished. This is a stated intention, not a decision with a tariff.

Since 1 November 2023 cameras check licence plates at the car-free pedestrian zone of the centre instead of automatic bollards; only vehicles with an exemption may enter, and visitors are told to park in garages or spaces around the inner city. Loading without a permit is allowed Monday to Friday 07:00-11:00 in the centre.

The municipality sells garage subscriptions for Doorneind and Boscotondo (page read on 21 October 2026): residents' 24/7 in Doorneind 47.50 euros per month, business 24/7 98.70, regular hours 85.30, office hours 71.80 and 24/7 in either garage 125.90 euros (2026 prices). Resident places are limited with a waiting list; entry is by licence-plate scanning during opening hours, and Doorneind closes at 21:00-22:00 on most days.

The council approved an investment of 21.2 million euros for the purchase and extension of the Elzas parking garage in early April 2025, to be earned back through parking revenue. The VVD criticised it as an expensive fix for street spaces removed earlier without a timely alternative.
items.source_title: Uitbreiding en aankoop ondergrondse parkeergarage Elzas Passage miljoenenproject (Ditishelmond.nl)

items.text: The Piet Blomplein page (read on 21 October 2026) says the Elzas garage is to be extended by about 250 spaces under the square, with construction starting in 2028 and taking over a year and a half, plus more than 310 homes above. The existing garage stays open during the works and the plan still needs council approval.

The municipality expects to place about 250 extra public charge points until 2028, in phases; phase 3 was being installed and phase 5 is open for comment until 28 October with installation planned for spring/summer 2027 (page read on 21 October 2026, undated).

In April 2025 the alderman said the new parking guidance system would first point only to the municipal garages Boscotondo and Doorneind and not to the privately run Elzas garage because its access route would change repeatedly. The Centrum 2030 page lists the guidance system among finished projects (read 21 October 2026).
items.source_title: Parkeergarage Elzas Passage 'voorlopig niet' meegenomen in parkeerverwijssysteem (Ditishelmond.nl)

items.text: Stadsparkeren states that in Helmond the Gepast Parkeren/Stadsparkeren card can no longer be used for street parking from 1 October 2026 because the card readers rely on the 2G network, which is being shut down. Street parking continues by app, and the card still works in connected garages including entry by licence-plate recognition (page read on 21 October 2026).

Q-Park lists P+R Smalstraat at the station as 170 spaces, open 24 hours, with a 2.10 m clearance, licence-plate recognition and disabled bays; its tariff table failed to load (page read on 21 October 2026). The rail-traveller discount applies for a domestic train journey with a return exit from the P+R on the same day.

NS lists Helmond P+R Smalstraat at 0.99 euros per hour, 6.00 euros per day and 4.00 euros for a rail traveller's day rate (including VAT, valid from 1 May 2026). The same sheet notes a summer promotion of at most 2 euros per day for rail travellers from 21 June to 31 August.

gaps: Capacities of the municipal garages Boscotondo (279) and Doorneind (470) and of the Elzas garage (195) could not be confirmed from any page opened; the Centrum 2030 map page (helmond.nl/1/welkom-bij-helmond/beheer/meta/parkeren-in-helmond-centrum) loads garage data by script and gave no figures.

Current garage hourly rates and daily maximum for Boscotondo, Doorneind and Elzas were not found on an official page; the only figures seen were on parking-listing portals (centrumparkeren.nl), which are not used.
Consolidated Uitvoeringsbesluit betaald- en vergunninghoudersparkeren Helmond 2015 (tariff class locations, paid-parking hours) not read in full; only the 2025 and 2026 amendment notices were opened.

No budget or council paper was found for the 2027 paid-parking extension (De Waart, Kasteel Noord, Suytkade, Annabuurt); only the Centrum 2030 statement of intention. The 2026 draft budget was not located.

No official garage occupancy statistics or published utilisation figures were found beyond the qualitative statements in the Strategie Parkeren; the strategy says garage data is compiled monthly internally.
The IP Parking client story on Helmond (https://www.ipparking.com/en/about-us/client-stories/municipality-of-helmond/) returned 403 and was not opened.

Omroep Brabant's article on the end of the pass readers was not used because it labels itself as automatically compiled; the Stadsparkeren flyer PDF was not used because its file metadata states AI-generated content.

Station-area plans (Stationskwartier, new station garage or Kluisstraat garage) were seen only in the Strategie Parkeren outline; no dedicated council decision or operator page was read. The NS station page for Helmond did not show parking information in readable form.

A 2021 consultant report (Actualisatie parkeerbeleid Helmond, July 2021, hosted on woo.helmond.nl) was read in part and mentions removing about 650 street spaces in the centre and an Elzas extension of about 230 spaces, but it is not used as an item because later pages give a figure of about 250.
